summary: The impossibility assertion is proved without mathematical errors or gaps. The reduced-basis geometry bounds the number of short and empty rows, which makes the sum of row maxima vanish under the shortest-vector score assumption. The chord-integral approximation is log-concave and converges in total variation to the row marginal, including the empty-row contribution. The parity comparison preserves original-mass canonical sampling, and the one-dimensional separation estimate and mode-centered compactness argument force concentration on two adjacent rows. Their primitive width-one slab has original root mass tending to one, contradicting the accepted original-root slab bound. All predecessor normalizations, affine cosets, parity classes, and auxiliary conditioning maps are consistent. The cell integration formula is exact, and the stated boundary conclusions follow vacuously from the proved impossibility, as explicitly claimed.
